prompt.context: Your client is an up-and-coming fintech startup that has reached a critical juncture in developing its main product, a machine-learning based platform that will be used by banks to improve their decision-making about whether to accept or reject loan applications. The CEO is wondering if a certain capability should be added to the platform or not.
prompt.question: How would you help the CEO think about whether to add this new capability to the platform?

clarifying_info.q: What new feature/capability is the CEO considering adding?
What is the startup's goal here?
clarifying_info.a: Maximize potential revenue and sales opportunities within reason.

clarifying_info.q: How does the startup plan to make money?
What is the financial situation of the startup?
clarifying_info.a: We will get to that later if it becomes relevant.

exhibits.title: Customer Feature Preferences Survey by Bank Size
exhibits.shows: A table rating how necessary various product features are, broken down by bank size (total assets), rated on a scale of 1 (not at all necessary) to 5 (essential). One of the features rated is the bias detection capability.
exhibits.data: Ratings for each feature across bank size segments: <$100M, $100M-$1B, $1B-$250B, >$250B; scale 1-5

exhibits.title: Sales Leads and Willingness to Pay by Bank Size
exhibits.shows: A table showing, for each bank size segment, the number of sales leads and the projected willingness to pay per sale.

exhibits.title: Startup Cumulative Spending Over Time (Before Project)
exhibits.shows: A chart showing the startup's cumulative cash spending over months, with a change in slope indicating when the team size changed. Total funding is $3M; 92% has been allocated.
exhibits.data: Total funding: $3M; 92% allocated; slope changes at month 2 (2 engineers added); spend rate month 0-2: $50k/month; spend rate month 2-12: $70k/month

exhibits.title: Bias Detection Project Requirements
exhibits.shows: A table or note specifying the engineering resources and timeline required to complete the bias detection project: number of engineers needed and duration of the project.
exhibits.data: 3 engineers required; 11 months to complete project

framework: 1. Banks (customers) — Do they want/need the bias detection feature? Which segment is most important for revenue? What is their WTP and price sensitivity?

2. Fintech startup (client) — Financials: development costs (# engineers, salary, project duration), cash on hand (available funds, burn rate), and sources of funding (VC, bank loan, personal). Non-financial: coding expertise and timeline/business needs.
3. Bias detection capability (product) — Is it compatible with the existing ML product? How easy is it to integrate?
4. Risks — Running out of funding, development delays angering investors, regulatory risks.
Process: First determine if potential customers want the feature, then calculate project cost, assess whether funding is sufficient, and if not brainstorm ways to raise capital.

questions.prompt: Do our potential customers want the bias detection capability? Which customer segment should we prioritize?
questions.guidance: Candidate should ask for customer preference data (Exhibit 1) and then seek segmentation/revenue data (Exhibit 2). From Exhibit 1: bias detection is rated low importance for <$100M and $100M-$1B banks, but high importance (must-have) for $1B-$250B and >$250B banks. Candidate must then ask which segment drives the most revenue. From Exhibit 2 calculations, the $1B-$250B segment is ~60% of projected revenue — so its preferences are paramount. Conclusion: the bias detection feature is critical and should be developed unless cost is prohibitive.

math.setup: For each bank size segment, calculate projected revenue = (# leads) x (WTP per sale), then compute each segment's share of total projected revenue.
math.answer: $1B-$250B banks are the largest revenue segment at ~61% of projected sales, followed by <$100M banks at ~31%. $100M-$1B and >$250B together account for only ~9%.

questions.prompt: How much will the bias detection project cost, and does the startup have sufficient funds?
questions.guidance: Candidate should ask about current available funds and project cost. Use Exhibits 3a and 3b together. Key insight: determine the per-engineer monthly cost by analyzing the change in spending slope when 2 engineers were added. Then apply that rate to the project specifications. Candidate should identify a $90K funding gap.

math.setup: Step 1: Calculate available funds from Exhibit 3a. Step 2: Determine per-engineer monthly cost from the change in spending slope. Step 3: Calculate total project cost using Exhibit 3b specs. Step 4: Compute the gap.
steps: Available funds: 8% of $3M total funding (since 92% is allocated) = 0.08 x $3,000,000 = $240,000
Increase in monthly spend when 2 engineers added: $70K - $50K = $20K/month
Cost per engineer per month: $20K / 2 engineers = $10,000/engineer/month
Project cost: 3 engineers x 11 months x $10,000 = $330,000
math.answer: Available funds: $240K. Project cost: $330K. The startup is $90K short of the funds needed to complete the project.

brainstorming.prompt: Brainstorm some ways the startup can get the necessary $90K in funding to add the bias detection capability to the platform.

categories.name: Internal sources
ideas: CEO and other founders/employees personally fund the venture and reimburse themselves once revenue is earned
Offer engineers equity or a percentage of future profits instead of paying full cash upfront
Reallocate a portion of the current budget toward this critical project
Cut costs elsewhere to free up the necessary funds (e.g., reduce discretionary spending, delay non-critical hires)

categories.name: External sources
ideas: VC fundraising — re-engage existing investors and explain the strategic importance of the feature
Seek a new strategic partnership that could bring capital or shared development costs
Crowdfunding campaign targeted at fintech/financial inclusion community
Bank loans or other debt financing
Government grants related to fair lending and bias reduction in financial services

recommendation: The client SHOULD develop the bias detection capability.
The $1B-$250B bank segment comprises ~61% of projected revenue, and bias detection is a must-have feature for that segment. Proceeding is strategically necessary.

Since the project costs $330K and only $240K is available, the startup must secure an additional $90K — either from internal reallocation or external funding sources (VC, bank loan, personal investment, etc.).
risks: Project costs and timeline could exceed projections, potentially delaying product launch and angering investors
Sales leads are projections; actual WTP and segment mix could differ materially from estimates — the $1B-$250B segment may prove less dominant than modeled
Competitors may enter the market and change the pricing dynamics before the feature is complete
next_steps: Assemble a team of 3 software engineers to complete the project within the 11-month timeline
Secure the additional $90K through an internal source (budget reallocation, cost cuts) and/or external source (VC re-engagement, bank loan)
Monitor project milestones and burn rate closely to avoid overruns
